From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>

Hi Claire — appreciate the context and the forecast. We can definitely support a mid-contract capacity increase and have three practical paths depending on what matters most to SupplyByte (cash smoothing vs. price concession vs. commitment length). High level:

Option A — Immediate top-up (fastest)
- Add 30% capacity on 2027-07-01, billed pro-rata on next invoice.
- No additional commitment term; unit rates unchanged.
- Pros: simplest; immediate throughput. Cons: single mid-cycle invoice.

Option B — Smoothed top-up (recommended if you want to avoid cash spike)
- We provision top-up immediately but convert the added spend into a 9-month staged commitment (aligns to your remaining term).
- Billing: monthly amortization of the incremental commitment (equal monthly charges) starting the next invoice cycle.
- Discount: 10% off incremental units if you sign the 9-month staged commitment.
- Pros: smooth cash impact; Redwood gets predictable incremental revenue.

Option C — Annualize & co-term (if you'd like longer protection)
- Convert incremental capacity into a full 12-month add-on that co-terms on your existing renewal date (effective 2027-07-01 through your renewal).
- Discount: 15% on incremental units for full annualization. Requires amendment signature and standard revenue recognition schedule.

I've attached a short spreadsheet with worked examples (monthly amounts, example invoice lines, and estimated TCO) so you can see dollarized impact at your current usage band. See attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Scenarios_0518.xlsx.

If you prefer, we can also structure a voucher/credit (one-time credit applied across invoices) instead of a price discount — that helps us preserve unit pricing while giving you effective cost relief.

Next steps: tell me which option you prefer (A/B/C), or confirm if procurement prefers a voucher instead of discount and I will pull finance in to finalize the amendment language. Happy to join a 30-min call this week.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Scenarios_0518.xlsx (xlsx, 78KB)

Ben / Markus — forwarding SupplyByte's ask and the options I proposed (see below). Key deal nuance: they want to avoid one large mid-cycle invoice. SupplyByte has 9 months left on their term. Seeking guidance on what we can approve without exec sign-off.

My read: they will likely prefer smoothing (Option B) but may push for the 15% annualized co-term discount (Option C). My recommended commercial: offer Option B + voucher credit instead of headline % if they push on price — e.g., 7.5% equivalent credit spread across the amortization months. That keeps list unit price intact and limits revenue haircut.

Ben: what discount floor do we want to allow? Markus: any constraints from rev rec / finance on how we amortize a voucher vs straight discount for accounting?

Soojin — fine to approve but keep it conservative. My guidance:
- Approve Option B (staged 9-month amortization) as standard for midterm smoothing.
- Offer a commercial concession equivalent to 7.5% (voucher credit) on incremental spend, applied monthly over the 9-month amortization. Avoid changing unit list price.

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Mid-contract headroom request + billing smoothing options

Agree with Ben with a small accounting caveat. Voucher-credit spread across invoices is operationally easiest, but:
- For accounting we need a clear amortization schedule in the amendment (we treat voucher as contra-revenue and amortize over the staged commitment months). That reduces recognized revenue in the period but is doable.
- If the customer requires an invoice-level discount (i.e., lower unit price), that triggers a modification to the contract and could affect ARR recognition. Avoid if possible.
- If SupplyByte prefers zero cash upfront, voucher + monthly amortization is OK. If they can prepay a portion, we can accelerate recognition and keep ARR cleaner.

Operational asks: include a line in the amendment that defines the "Incremental Capacity Voucher" amount and the exact invoicing schedule. Finance will prepare the amortization table once Soojin confirms numbers.

Markus
Head of Revenue Accounting
